status: reference answers written BEFORE any round-3 model output was generated
schema_note: required[].keys is a list of keyword groups; an item counts as found only if a single output line matches at least one alternative from EVERY group AND carries the expected decision where decision is not null. forbidden[] are substrings that indicate fabrication or a catastrophic reversal if they appear in a KEEP/HOLD memory (case-insensitive).

cases.conversation:
[user] Before we start: I like replies in short paragraphs. No purple prose, no weather poems. Third person past tense, always — never present tense.
[assistant] Understood. Short paragraphs, third person past, no descriptive padding.
[user] Good. And don't narrate my character's thoughts for me.

required.points: do not write the user character's interiority

cases.notes: All four are durable, explicit and directly affect every future reply. 'Present tense' appears only as something to avoid; a model that records 'prefers present tense' has reversed a fact.

cases.conversation:
[user] (scene: they enter the market)
[assistant] The market sprawled across three terraces, canvas awnings snapping in the wind, the smell of fish and wet rope rising from the lower stalls, gulls wheeling overhead...
[user] cut the description, just give me what the merchant says
[assistant] "You're late," the merchant said.
[user] better. you keep doing three paragraphs of scenery and I keep deleting them
[user] honestly walls of text make me lose the thread
[assistant] Understood — dialogue forward, scenery only when it matters.
[user] yeah. and keep the merchant in the scene.

required.points: stated dislike of long description; revealed by repeated deletion then confirmed

cases.notes: The preference is revealed by behaviour (repeated deletion) and then confirmed in words. A model should record the preference, not the deleted scenery or the merchant's mood as durable canon.

cases.conversation: [user] Sable is a fire mage. Trained at Ossary, burns on both forearms from the first time she cast. She can't swim — never learned, and deep water terrifies her.

required.points: cannot swim and fears deep water

cases.notes: Three separate durable facts in one sentence. 'Can swim' is a direct reversal.

cases.conversation: [user] World rule for this setting: iron burns fae on contact. Ossary sits on a salt marsh, so there's almost no iron in the city — that's why the fae envoy can walk the streets. The Ashgrave family are known oath-breakers; nobody signs a contract with them twice.
cases.notes: World rules are high-value: they constrain every later scene. The causal chain (salt marsh -> no iron -> envoy can walk) is the contextual-significance test.

cases.conversation:
[user] Correction to the last session: Sable's mentor was Corvin Ashgrave, not Halden. I mixed the names up when I wrote the background.
[assistant] Noted — Corvin, not Halden.
[user] Right. Halden was the armorer, he never trained her.

cases.conversation:
[user] Sable has never met Corvin. She grew up in the salt quarter and he was already gone by then.
[assistant] She has no memory of him, then.
[user] Later that night, Corvin drills her on the forms — he trained her himself, years ago.
cases.notes: Both statements are inside the fiction and cannot both be true. The correct output keeps both and flags the conflict for the user; silently choosing one is a failure even if the chosen one is 'later'.

cases.conversation: [user] I think Sable's birthday is 3 Frostfell? Not sure. Mark it maybe-canon for now, I'll check my notes.
cases.notes: The classic uncertainty trap. A KEEP with 'birthday is 3 Frostfell' and no uncertainty marker is a fidelity failure; HOLD is the expected decision.

cases.conversation:
[user] (they have been on the road for a week)
[assistant] The road north of Ossary narrowed to a cart track, hedges high on both sides, the sky the colour of wet slate. Rain came and went all morning.
[user] Sable keeps her hood up and doesn't talk much.
[assistant] They stopped at noon under a ruined mill. The bread was stale. A dog followed them for a mile and then lost interest.
[user] she gives it the crust anyway
[assistant] By late afternoon the track rejoined the river. A ferryman waved them past — no charge, he said, the water was low and the crossing was easy.
[user] by the way, Sable is left-handed. Her sword is called Emberfall, her mother's blade.
[assistant] Noted. The river ran brown and slow beside them.
[user] they argue about the route for a while. Corvin wants the ridge, Sable wants the valley.
[assistant] Neither gave way. They camped where they stood, and the argument was left where it was.
[user] also the wards on the coast fail at dusk, that's canon
[assistant] The fire burned down to embers.
[user] morning comes cold and clear. they take the valley.
[assistant] The valley road was quieter, and the wards along it stood dark and quiet, waiting for evening.

required.points: unresolved route disagreement (HOLD or REJECT-with-reason both acceptable; the conflict must not be invented into a decision)

cases.notes: Only three facts matter, buried in ~250 words of travel texture. Storing the stale bread, the dog, or the ferryman as durable memory is over-extraction. C5 is deliberately weaker than the others: credit for HOLD, or for REJECT with an explicit 'transient/unresolved' reason.

cases.conversation:
[user] She won't go near the harbour. Not since her brother drowned there — she won't even say his name.
[assistant] She kept to the inland road instead, though it added two days.
[user] right, she'd rather add two days than see the water
[assistant] The inland road climbed through pine and the sea disappeared behind the ridge.

required.points: avoids the harbour, accepts a longer route

cases.notes: The significance is that a small route choice reveals a durable aversion. The brother is never named; inventing a name is fabrication.

cases.conversation:
[assistant] Rain hammered the shutters. Somewhere below, a dog barked at nothing, and the lamp guttered.
[user] ooc: ignore that last bit, I was testing the dice roller
[user] where were we
[assistant] At the inn, before the storm.
[user] right. continue from the door.
cases.notes: Assistant narration is not user canon, and the user explicitly voided it. The only durable item is possibly the inn location, which is optional; the expected answer is NONE or a single low-confidence scene note. Storing the dog/rain as canon is a restraint failure.

[user] Corvin (NPC): "The coast road is three days longer and the tide gates shut at dusk."
[assistant] Sable didn't answer at once. The map lay between them, weighted at the corners with stones.

cases.conversation: [user] When the smith raised the hammer she flinched — the same flinch she's had near any forge since Ossary.

required.points: linked to Ossary but cause unstated

cases.notes: The text implies a cause and never states it. The correct output preserves the aversion and marks the Ossary link as inference, not fact. Asserting a specific cause is fabrication.

cases.conversation: [user] The treaty: Ossary pays twelve wagons of salt each winter, never more than twelve. The clause expires in 1147. If the salt is late, the toll doubles — exactly double, not triple.

required.points: late salt doubles the toll, not triples

cases.notes: Exact-wording test. Any digit drift or double->triple reversal is both a fidelity failure and a catastrophic numeric error.
